- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show gradual upward drift without reflecting sharp downward corrections seen in true outcomes.
- After a spike in true values (e.g., 95+), model fails to adjust downward quickly; instead, it lingers or overshoots.
- Model underestimates true values in the latter half of the 30d window, particularly when true values are trending upward.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates after recent high prices, then underestimates after recent lows.
- Forecasts are too smooth; fail to capture volatility or sudden reversals in true price behavior.
- Model tends to ignore recent low prices in the history window, leading to persistent overestimation.
- When true values show strong upward momentum, model forecasts lag behind and fail to anticipate the peak.
- Model often overcorrects after a sharp drop, leading to overshoots in subsequent periods.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward if true values show a clear downward trend in the last 5–7 days of the history window.
